clue.text: Six rulers are Norsemen

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: A claim that six monarchs were Scandinavian warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were the seafaring raiders and traders of medieval Scandinavia, the Norsemen of history.

clue.text: Former lover putting on a French green top

indicators.note: in a down clue the former lover is set below, so the French word sits on top of it

parts.note: vert is French for green
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex-partner dons a green French hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertex is the highest point or apex of a shape, so it means the top.

clue.text: One in bed that's smoked

definitions.meaning: a ..., from British slang kip, sleep, is one who sleeps
a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Someone smoking in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: To kip is British slang for to sleep; a kipper is also a split, smoked herring eaten for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Kippers are herrings cured by smoking, and in slang a kipper is someone having a kip.

clue.text: Hopeless course, main meal or pudding suggested

definitions.meaning: an idea or plan with no chance of success
a main or a pudding is a dinner course that is not a starter

explanation.surface: A diner is offered a doomed menu of mains or desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' first reads as a plan of action, then as part of a meal: mains and puddings are courses other than the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is a proposal or plan bound to fail, a course of action with no prospects.

clue.text: Parable of small man in debt

definitions.note: the parable of the sower is a story told by Jesus in the Gospels

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
one who owes is an ower

explanation.surface: A Bible story about a minor figure who owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a title: the Parable of the Sower, about seed falling on good and bad ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus's story of a farmer scattering seed is known as the Parable of the Sower, completing the phrase.

clue.text: Threatening to have no more room for packages?

definitions.meaning: menacing or threatening harm

definitions.text: to have no more room for packages?
definitions.meaning: read as BALE FULL: a store of bales, bundled packages of hay or goods, with no space left

explanation.surface: Someone sounds menacing because the parcels have nowhere left to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into BALE and FULL; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A baleful look is a menacing one, full of ill intent, so it suits threatening as an adjective.

clue.text: Leave play but maintain contact

definitions.meaning: a ball that is in touch has gone over the side line and out of play, in rugby or football
to keep in contact

explanation.surface: Advice to quit the theatre yet keep phoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama; it is the field of play, and touch is the area beyond the side lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in touch means keeping up communication, and a ball in touch has crossed out of the pitch.

clue.text: Free ride that takes one up and down

definitions.meaning: a ride given free in someone's car

definitions.text: that takes one up and down
definitions.meaning: a British elevator

explanation.surface: A complimentary trip that rises and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift is the British word for an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a lift means driving them without charge, and a lift also carries people between floors.

clue.text: Sick conifers get such investigation

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing an investigation, so 'such' points back to the anagram's result

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters of conifers are unwell, out of their healthy order

explanation.surface: Ailing pine trees are subjected to scientific examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'such investigation' means investigation of this kind: the answer describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic work applies scientific methods to crime, as in forensic examination of evidence.

clue.text: Not to mention being undisturbed

definitions.meaning: not to mention, much less
left untouched, not disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet about a person who wants peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces something even less likely, much less, and also means left in peace.

clue.text: Approach maturity in state prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a pen is an enclosure, slang for a prison (penitentiary)

explanation.surface: An inmate grows up while serving time in a state jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a containment signal: the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or plans that ripen come close to full development, so the verb means nearing maturity.

clue.text: Hang on: one way to get a tip?

definitions.meaning: a call to be patient, to hang on a moment

definitions.text: one way to get a tip?
definitions.meaning: a waiter who waits for a gratuity is, punningly, waiting for it

explanation.surface: A tip-hungry waiter is told to be patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading plays on waiting at table, the job that earns tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken plea for patience, as when someone builds up to a punchline: hang on.

clue.text: Choose to speak for everyone on the register

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak formally, make a speech

explanation.surface: Someone picks a spokesperson to represent all who are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of voters, all those named on the electoral roll.

clue.text: One facing op may have to take this by mouth

definitions.text: One facing op may have to take this by mouth

parts.words: One facing op may have to take this by mouth
parts.note: before surgery, hospitals forbid patients any food or drink; the sign above the bed names the quantity allowed orally

explanation.surface: A pre-surgery patient told what to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the thing taken by mouth is nothing at all, from the hospital instruction 'nil by mouth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, and the hospital sign before an operation forbids taking any food or drink orally.

clue.text: Hard labour to created user guide?

definitions.meaning: physical labour done by hand
writing a manual, a user guide, is work on a manual

explanation.surface: Toil sentenced to someone who wrote an instruction booklet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard labour' looks like a prison sentence; it means physically demanding work.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual work is labour with the hands, physically tiring, while a manual is also a handbook.

clue.text: Clear speech launches ritual action

indicators.note: launches suggests sending the letters of ritual action flying off into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Crisp oratory sets a ceremonial act in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulation is the distinct pronouncing of sounds, the quality of crisp, well-formed speaking.

clue.text: Train is awfully nice: try it!

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of nice try it are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A rail advert urges travellers to sample a pleasant service.
explanation.walkthrough: InterCity is the British brand for fast long-distance trains between cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An InterCity is an express service linking major British cities, so it is a kind of train.

clue.text: Socialist to abandon Worcestershire seat

parts.note: red describes a left-winger or socialist
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: A left-wing MP walks away from a constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: Redditch is a town and parliamentary constituency in Worcestershire, an English Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: Redditch is a parliamentary constituency in Worcestershire, so it is a seat in the electoral sense.

clue.text: Write name on official building

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a name or label
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to inscribe a label on a government office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a positional link but supplies its own letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, a famous government building.

clue.text: Latest possible moment for silently remembering the Armistice?

definitions.meaning: the last moment before it is too late
the First World War ended at the ... of 11 November, marked each year by a silence at 11 am

explanation.surface: A late plea to remember the end of the Great War quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remembrance Day in Britain is observed with a two-minute silence at 11 am, the hour the 1918 Armistice took effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at the eleventh hour means doing it at the last minute, just before a deadline.

clue.text: I am about to study young woman

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these two words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Someone is about to start learning, a girl perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to study' reads as 'ready to start studying', but 'about' turns 'I am' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned word for a girl or unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Belittle church dignitary who's holding me up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the cleric grips the next piece

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric of a cathedral

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word me reads bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A cleric who blocks my path disparages me.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads 'me' bottom to top; 'who's holding' puts that inside the cleric. A dean heads a cathedral chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, to belittle or humiliate them.

clue.text: What's the point in Herodotus?

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted sit inside the Greek historian's name

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks the purpose of studying an ancient historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the point' sounds like a complaint about reading Herodotus; it is a request for a point, a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a point, as in a full stop or decimal point.

clue.text: Unofficial show for prisoner near end of sentence?

definitions.meaning: a screening or issue before the official launch
read as ..., the state of an inmate about to be freed

explanation.surface: An informal performance staged for an inmate whose term is almost up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' is a prison term, not a line of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-release screening or version comes out ahead of the formal launch, so it is not yet the official show.

clue.text: Tory not initially intelligent

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: bright means intelligent

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Conservative lacks brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially intelligent' reads as an insult; it removes the first letter of BRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The right is the conservative side of politics, so a Tory is of the right.

clue.text: Starts off hostilities, a Kiwi activity

definitions.text: Starts off hostilities, a Kiwi activity

indicators.note: starts off means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A New Zealand ritual begins proceedings with aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition; a Kiwi is a New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori war dance, famously performed by New Zealand's rugby team before a match.

clue.text: A measure of warmth in the direction of drain cover

definitions.meaning: a ... measures how warm a duvet is

definitions.text: in the direction of drain cover
definitions.meaning: towards a grating, the grille over a drain

explanation.surface: Heat seems to flow towards the grille over a gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The tog is a British unit of thermal insulation printed on duvets and quilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tog ratings grade bedding by insulation, so a higher figure means a warmer duvet.

clue.text: Magazine I dole out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of I dole are put out of order

explanation.surface: A publisher hands out copies of a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British humorous magazine aimed at older readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oldie is a well-known British monthly, so it is a specific example of a magazine.

clue.text: Very eager to tour a country

indicators.note: to tour means to go around, so the eager word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: hungry means very eager, as in hungry for success

explanation.surface: Someone longs to travel round a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary is a landlocked nation in central Europe, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Engaged one tank in action

indicators.note: in action says the letters of one tank are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier reports one armoured vehicle joined battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' looks military, fitting the tank; it means hired or taken into employment.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken someone on is to have hired them, so engaged in the employment sense fits.
